subject: Kickoff: NovaHealth Dedicated GPU Pool provisioning & burst policy
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@novahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — kickoff + a few clarifying questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We landed internally on pursuing a dedicated GPU pool with Redwood to support our inference traffic for our EU deployment. Before the kickoff I'd like to align on a few operational items so we can have the right folks on the call:

- Desired steady-state pool: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (we may scale to 12 for peak).
- Expected peak traffic profile: 400 concurrent requests, avg 6 messages per session, typical prompt length ~1.2k tokens.
- Data residency: all model inputs/outputs must remain in EU region.
- Compliance ask: brief SOC2 + network peering checklist for our security team.

Can you share a rough mutual action plan and what defaults Redwood would recommend for autoscale and burst? Also please attach any provisioning templates we should fill out ahead of the kickoff.

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager — Machine Intelligence
NovaHealth

Attachments: none in this message
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@novahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — kickoff + a few clarifying questions

Sara — great to hear, and congrats on the green light. High level response and a proposed MAP below. I've attached our provisioning template for the team to complete (provisioning_template.xlsx).

Quick answers:
- Region/data residency: we can pin everything to eu-west-1 and enforce no cross-region failover unless explicitly enabled in the config.
- Autoscale recommendation (starter): target 8 GPUs steady, autoscale up to 12 based on 60s sustained queue depth > 25; burst allowance to 16 for 10-minute windows with higher cost tier. We can tighten thresholds after 2 weeks of production telemetry.
- Burst policy note: bursts are best-effort capacity that may incur routing to a secondary pool if primary exhausted; we'll include fallbacks in the MAP.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) This week: internal kickoffs + provisioning template completed by NovaHealth (owner: Sara).
2) Week 1: Redwood creates preliminary pool in eu-west-1 (soft standby), network peering workshop with NovaNetwork (owner: Ben Carter).
3) Week 2: Test traffic (staging), autoscale threshold tuning, KV cache priming (owner: Grace O'Connor).
4) Week 3: Go/no-go + production cutover, monitoring and SLO hooks configured (owner: Marissa Cole).

Ask: can you confirm the target go-live window (we have capacity windows on 10/4 and 10/18 in eu region)? Also share the SOW contact for signatures so we can prefill the doc.

I'll book a 45-min kickoff for next Tuesday and include a short ops/peering agenda.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical notes so NovaHealth can prepare details ahead of the kickoff:

- Model variants: please list which model families you plan to serve (e.g., LlamaX-70B / opt-30b / custom finetuned checkpoints). Kernel selection and quantization guidance depends on architecture.
- Token distribution: average vs 95th percentile sequence lengths — if 95th > 4k we should size for KV cache memory accordingly.
- Expected request QPS and peak tokens/sec (not just concurrent requests) — helps set batching targets.
- Networking: will NovaHealth use IPsec site-to-site, or a cloud peering/VPC endpoint? If peering, we'll need subnet CIDR ranges and ingress ACL contacts.
- Maintenance windows: propose Sundays 02:00–05:00 UTC as default; please flag if unacceptable.

Internal notes for Redwood team (internal-only):
- Grace: lead kernel/quantization recommendations post model list.
- Ben: coordinate peering and netops checklist; confirm MTR/traceroute pre-cutover.
- Marissa: CS runbook and customer-facing runbook drafts.

Thanks,
Grace
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Maintenance window OK for Sunday 02:00–05:00 UTC.

SOW contact: Tim Rogers (tim.rogers@cloudbroker.io) — he handles procurement and signing.
